#!/bin/sh
# Session 8 (2026-11-09): the learner (a warehouse picker) asked for real freight instead of tidy identical cartons:
# odd sizes mixed inside a layer, non-box shapes (sacks, shrink-wrapped tin trays, a long carton), and the pallet
# sitting on a ride-on pallet jack. No avatar: on Specs the wearer is the picker. Rebuild, re-test, re-record.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." || exit 1
claude -p "$(cat <<'PROMPT'
Lens Studio is open with this project (Stack Right; devpost/design-brief.md is the approved brief). Work through the CLAD skills and the Lens Studio MCP. Bash and ffmpeg (C:/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe) are available. Read Assets/Scripts/*.ts first; StackRightPickList.ts owns the order and the computed plan.

The learner (who picks real store orders) reviewed the demo: every case is a tidy identical carton, which is not what real freight looks like. Make the order realistic. Keep every existing rule, interaction, the ghost/tag/snap/tip/card behaviour, the demo driver and the tests working.

1. New order (replace ORDER_LINES; still heaviest first; sizes W x D x H cm; every case in a layer has the same H so each layer finishes level):
   - Layer 1: PET FOOD 20kg, 20 kg, w 55, d 37, h 14, count 6, shape "sack".
   - Layer 2: LAUNDRY 4x4L, 17 kg, w 38, d 58, h 30, count 6, shape "carton".
   - Layer 3 (MIXED, turned 90): WATER 24, 14 kg, w 38, d 58, h 25, count 4, carton; then JUICE 12x1L, 12 kg, w 38, d 29, h 25, count 4, carton. Turned, water is 58 across x 38 deep, 2 per row, 2 rows; the juice fills the leftover 38 cm strip, 4 across.
   - Layer 4: TINNED TOMATOES 2x24, 10 kg, w 57, d 38, h 13, count 6, shape "tray" (2 per row, 3 rows).
   - Layer 5 (MIXED, fragile on top): BREAD, 4 kg, w 56, d 45, h 30, count 2; PAPER TOWEL 12, 3 kg, w 112, d 25, h 30, count 1, shape "long" carton; CHIPS, 2 kg, w 56, d 45, h 30, count 2.
   Total 31 cases, deck 15 + 14+30+25+13+30 = 127 cm.
   Pick bright, light colours per line (additive display, no dark colours); keep fragile flags for bread and chips.

2. Plan stays computed, not hand-placed. Replace the one-footprint grid with row (shelf) packing per layer: take the layer's cases in order, footprint per line (turned per layer, so put a per-line or per-layer turned flag in the data instead of TURNED_LAYERS=[2,4]; layer 3 is turned), fill a row left to right while it fits 116.5 cm, start a new row nearer the user when it doesn't, row depth = deepest case in it; centre each row in x and the whole layer in z. Print an error if a layer overflows the pallet or mixes heights. The joints of each layer should cross the one below: check the plan does that for this order and say so in the report.
   The layer-done note is now per layer, two lines, true for the plan, e.g. "Layer 2 done.\nNext layer turns 90° so the joints cross." vs "Layer 3 done.\nFlat trays next: keep the top level." Write them to be accurate for each layer.

3. Shapes, built from primitives/mesh builder (no new material assets without a shader; reuse the existing case materials/BoxFactory pattern):
   - sack: a soft, rounded, pillow-like bag (e.g. a flattened, slightly squashed ellipsoid/capsule or a stack of 2-3 shrinking rounded slabs with a crimped seam at the ends). It must not read as a sharp cube.
   - tray: a low cardboard tray (about 4 cm lip) with the tins visible as a grid of short cylinders on top of it, plus a faint clear shrink-wrap box around it.
   - long: an ordinary carton but 112 cm long, so it reads as the odd one.
   - carton: as now.
   Labels (name + kg + HEAVY/FRAGILE) still readable on every shape. The ghost can stay the wire bounding box of the footprint. Grab colliders = the bounding box. Make sure sacks, trays and the 112 cm carton sit on the pick face without poking through the shelf uprights (widen the shelf or the queue spacing if needed, keep it 1.4 m to the right).

4. Ride-on pallet jack: the pallet sits on the forks of a ride-on electric pallet jack (the kind an order picker stands on). Build it from primitives at real size: two forks under the pallet visible in the pallet's openings, the power unit (about 80 wide, 60 deep, 120 tall, safety yellow/orange, bright) at the pallet's edge on the side that does not block the user's view of the pallet, the pick face or the ghost, a small operator platform and a tiller/handle. It is scenery only (no physics, not grabbable, no game rules), and must not hide the Reset button, the counter, the tag, the tips or the completion card from the default position or the demo camera. The pallet keeps its current position and deck height so the plan and tests stay valid.

5. Demo driver ("demo" mode in StackRightTestDriver.ts): keep the beats and their [DEMO] log names: intro, case1, overhang, gap, case2, layer1, layer2, layer3mixed, fast, layer5, complete, reset, end. Changes: rename "layer2turn" to two beats: "layer2" (layer 2 at 0.9 s per case) and "layer3mixed" (first water case slow: 3 s carry, 1.5 s hover; rest of the water at 0.9 s; first juice case slow: 3 s carry, 1.5 s hover; rest of the juice at 0.9 s). "fast" = layer 4 at 0.5 s per case. "layer5" = layer 5 at 1.4 s per case but hover 1.5 s over the ghost for the long paper towel carton. Other beat timings unchanged. Default driver mode must be "off" when you finish.

6. Update the self-test driver checks and the LEAF scenarios (Assets/Tests and copies in devpost/leaf-scenarios) for the new order: 31 cases, 5 layers, 127 cm, tag text "Layer N · K of 31 · kg", per-layer done notes, the turned layer, plus new checks: the plan has no overlaps and stays inside the pallet; every layer is level; layer 3 and layer 5 contain more than one footprint. Run them; append results to devpost/selftest-2026-11-09.log. Everything must pass.

7. Look at it: CapturePanelScreenshotTool of the Preview at the demo camera, with the order at layer 1 (sacks), mid layer 3 (mixed + ghost), layer 4 (trays), and the completion card; save as devpost/screenshots/v4-*.png and check by eye that sacks read as sacks, trays show tins, the jack reads as a pallet jack, and nothing important is hidden. Fix what doesn't.

8. Re-record exactly as before (see devpost/agent-logs/run_demo_v4.sh steps 3-5 and the 06/07 transcripts for preview size, ffmpeg region and camera): ffmpeg gdigrab of the Preview panel, 30 fps, x264 crf 18, to devpost/video/raw_demo.mp4 (overwrite); record_start.txt with ms; all [DEMO] and [StackRight] lines to devpost/video/demo_beats.log; stop ffmpeg with q right after "[DEMO] end". Extract check frames devpost/video/check-*.png at case1 hover, overhang tip, gap tip, layer3mixed first-juice hover, layer5 paper-towel hover, completion card; look at each. Set the driver back to "off" and save the scene.

Known gotchas: injected mouse input does not register grabs; CaptureRuntimeViewTool and the preview-interaction package install can freeze Lens Studio; open pop-ups silently block the TypeScript compiler (if compiles stop reporting, say so instead of looping). Don't touch .agents/skills, .claude/skills or Plugins/. Units are cm; keep everything bright.

Do not git commit, push, or touch anything outside this project folder. When done, print a short report: what changed per file, the computed plan per layer (rows and footprints) and whether the joints cross, how each shape was built, where the jack is, test totals, recording path/length, demo beat times relative to recording start, what each check frame showed, and anything unfinished or that looks off.
PROMPT
)" --mcp-config .mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --permission-mode auto --output-format stream-json --verbose \
  > devpost/agent-logs/08-shapes-v6.jsonl 2> devpost/agent-logs/08-shapes-v6.err
echo "exit $?"

1	// StackRightPickList.ts
2	// STAND-IN FOR BARCODE SCAN. A real picker's Lens would read the case's barcode when it is
3	// picked up. For the preview, the order is fixed: 30 cases in the warehouse system's
4	// heaviest-first sequence (5 layers). The learner should replace these lines with real order lines.
5	//
6	// Owns: the order (case data: name, weight, class, real size in cm, colour) and the LOAD PLAN,
7	// which is generated in code from the case sizes (not hand-placed): each layer is a centred grid
8	// of as many cases as fit the 116.5 cm pallet, and layers 2 and 4 are turned 90 degrees so the
9	// joints don't line up (interlock). Pure data/logic, no scene access.
10	// Must not: touch the scene, hold game state.
11	//
12	// Case sizes are W (x) x H (y) x D (z) in cm, in the case's own frame. Plan positions are in
13	// Pallet-local cm: x right, z toward the user (near edge = +z), y up from the floor.
14	// Pallet deck top is at y = 15.
15	
16	export interface CaseSpec {
17	  key: string // used in scene object names, e.g. Case_03_Laundry
18	  name: string // printed on the case
19	  kg: number
20	  fragile: boolean // true = crushable, goes on top
21	  layer: number // 1..5
22	  size: vec3 // W x H x D, cm (case frame)
23	  color: vec4 // bright, light-saturated label colour (additive display: no dark colours)
24	}
25	
26	export interface PlannedSlot {
27	  center: vec3 // Pallet-local centre of the case when placed
28	  layer: number // 1..5
29	  turned: boolean // true = turned 90 degrees about up (case W runs along pallet z)
30	  row: number // 0 = far row
31	  col: number // 0 = left column
32	}
33	
34	export const PALLET_SIZE_CM = new vec3(116.5, 15, 116.5)
35	export const PALLET_DECK_Y = 15
36	export const HEIGHT_LIMIT_CM = 180
37	/** Layers that are turned 90 degrees relative to layer 1 (interlock). */
38	export const TURNED_LAYERS = [2, 4]
39	
40	interface OrderLine {key: string, name: string, kg: number, fragile: boolean, layer: number,
41	  w: number, d: number, h: number, count: number, color: vec4}
42	
43	// The order from devpost/design-brief.md, sizes W x D x H in cm, already heaviest first.
44	const ORDER_LINES: OrderLine[] = [
45	  {key: "Laundry", name: "LAUNDRY 4x4L", kg: 17, fragile: false, layer: 1, w: 38, d: 58, h: 30, count: 6, color: new vec4(0.6, 0.55, 1.0, 1)},
46	  {key: "Water", name: "WATER 24", kg: 14, fragile: false, layer: 2, w: 38, d: 58, h: 30, count: 6, color: new vec4(0.35, 0.75, 1.0, 1)},
47	  {key: "Tomatoes", name: "TOMATOES 24", kg: 10, fragile: false, layer: 3, w: 29, d: 58, h: 25, count: 8, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.4, 0.5, 1)},
48	  {key: "SoftDrink", name: "SOFT DRINK 24", kg: 9, fragile: false, layer: 4, w: 38, d: 58, h: 25, count: 6, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.6, 0.3, 1)},
49	  {key: "Eggs", name: "EGGS", kg: 10, fragile: true, layer: 5, w: 58, d: 58, h: 32, count: 1, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.92, 0.7, 1)},
50	  {key: "Bread", name: "BREAD", kg: 4, fragile: true, layer: 5, w: 58, d: 58, h: 32, count: 1, color: new vec4(1.0, 0.8, 0.5, 1)},
51	  {key: "Chips", name: "CHIPS", kg: 2, fragile: true, layer: 5, w: 58, d: 58, h: 32, count: 2, color: new vec4(0.5, 1.0, 0.6, 1)},
52	]
53	
54	function buildOrder(): CaseSpec[] {
55	  const out: CaseSpec[] = []
56	  for (const l of ORDER_LINES) {
57	    for (let k = 0; k < l.count; k++) {
58	      out.push({key: l.key, name: l.name, kg: l.kg, fragile: l.fragile, layer: l.layer,
59	        size: new vec3(l.w, l.h, l.d), color: l.color})
60	    }
61	  }
62	  return out
63	}
64	
65	export const ORDER: CaseSpec[] = buildOrder()
66	export const LAYER_COUNT = ORDER.reduce((m, c) => Math.max(m, c.layer), 0)
67	
68	export function isTurnedLayer(layer: number): boolean {
69	  return TURNED_LAYERS.indexOf(layer) >= 0
70	}
71	
72	/** Footprint on the pallet (x = across, z = depth) of a case in the planned orientation. */
73	export function footprint(spec: CaseSpec, turned: boolean): vec2 {
74	  return turned ? new vec2(spec.size.z, spec.size.x) : new vec2(spec.size.x, spec.size.z)
75	}
76	
77	/** Ghost / placed size in pallet axes: the case size with x and z swapped when turned. */
78	export function plannedSize(spec: CaseSpec, turned: boolean): vec3 {
79	  return turned ? new vec3(spec.size.z, spec.size.y, spec.size.x) : spec.size
80	}
81	
82	/**
83	 * Generates the slot plan for the whole order. For each layer: take the footprint of the layer's
84	 * case (turned 90 degrees on TURNED_LAYERS), fit as many as fit the pallet as a centred, tight
85	 * grid, fill far row to near row, left to right, and stack the layer on the previous layer's top.
86	 * Every case in a layer must share one footprint and height (out of scope: mixed layers).
87	 */
88	export function buildPlan(order: CaseSpec[]): PlannedSlot[] {
89	  const plan: PlannedSlot[] = []
90	  let bottom = PALLET_DECK_Y
91	  let i = 0
92	  while (i < order.length) {
93	    const layer = order[i].layer
94	    const first = order[i]
95	    const turned = isTurnedLayer(layer)
96	    const fp = footprint(first, turned)
97	    const cols = Math.floor(PALLET_SIZE_CM.x / fp.x)
98	    const rows = Math.floor(PALLET_SIZE_CM.z / fp.y)
99	    const x0 = -(cols * fp.x) / 2 + fp.x / 2
100	    const z0 = -(rows * fp.y) / 2 + fp.y / 2
101	    let n = 0
102	    while (i < order.length && order[i].layer === layer) {
103	      if (n >= cols * rows) {
104	        print("[StackRightPickList] ERROR: layer " + layer + " has more cases than fit (" + cols * rows + ")")
105	        break
106	      }
107	      const row = Math.floor(n / cols)
108	      const col = n % cols
109	      plan.push({
110	        center: new vec3(x0 + col * fp.x, bottom + first.size.y / 2, z0 + row * fp.y),
111	        layer, turned, row, col,
112	      })
113	      n++
114	      i++
115	    }
116	    while (i < order.length && order[i].layer === layer) i++ // skip any overflow
117	    bottom += first.size.y
118	  }
119	  return plan
120	}
121	
122	export const PLAN: PlannedSlot[] = buildPlan(ORDER)
123	
124	/** Top of the finished stack above the floor (cm). */
125	export const STACK_HEIGHT_CM = PLAN.reduce((m, s, k) => Math.max(m, s.center.y + ORDER[k].size.y / 2), PALLET_DECK_Y)
126	
127	/** Number of cases in each layer, index = layer. */
128	export function layerCaseCount(layer: number): number {
129	  let n = 0
130	  for (const c of ORDER) if (c.layer === layer) n++
131	  return n
132	}
133	
134	/** True when case i is the last one of its layer in the order. */
135	export function isLastOfLayer(i: number): boolean {
136	  return i < ORDER.length && (i === ORDER.length - 1 || ORDER[i + 1].layer !== ORDER[i].layer)
137	}
138	
139	export function ghostTagText(i: number): string {
140	  return "Layer " + ORDER[i].layer + " · " + (i + 1) + " of " + ORDER.length + " · " + ORDER[i].kg + " kg"
141	}
142	
143	export function layerDoneText(layer: number): string {
144	  return "Layer " + layer + " done.\nNext layer turns 90° so the joints don't line up."
145	}

1	// StackRightGeometry.ts
2	// Owns: tiny helpers that build primitive box visuals (pallet, shelves, cartons, ghost, arrow)
3	// from one 1 cm box mesh + one unlit material that is cloned per box. These are the obvious
4	// placeholder visuals; swap the boxMesh / baseMaterial @inputs on the controller to upgrade.
5	// Scale always lives on the leaf "Visual" child, never on a node that owns a collider.
6	// Must not: hold game state or create text.
7	
8	export class BoxFactory {
9	  constructor(private mesh: RenderMesh, private baseMaterial: Material) {}
10	
11	  makeMaterial(color: vec4, translucent: boolean): Material {
12	    const mat = this.baseMaterial.clone()
13	    mat.mainPass.baseColor = color
14	    if (translucent) {
15	      mat.mainPass.blendMode = BlendMode.Normal
16	      mat.mainPass.depthWrite = false
17	    }
18	    return mat
19	  }
20	
21	  /** Creates a child SceneObject with a box visual of `size` cm centred at `localPos`. */
22	  makeBox(parent: SceneObject, name: string, size: vec3, localPos: vec3, color: vec4,
23	    translucent: boolean = false): RenderMeshVisual {
24	    const so = global.scene.createSceneObject(name)
25	    so.setParent(parent)
26	    const t = so.getTransform()
27	    t.setLocalPosition(localPos)
28	    t.setLocalScale(size)
29	    const rmv = so.createComponent("Component.RenderMeshVisual") as RenderMeshVisual
30	    rmv.mesh = this.mesh
31	    rmv.mainMaterial = this.makeMaterial(color, translucent)
32	    return rmv
33	  }
34	
35	  /** 12 thin bars outlining a box of `size` centred at the parent's origin. */
36	  makeWireBox(parent: SceneObject, name: string, size: vec3, thickness: number, color: vec4): SceneObject {
37	    const root = global.scene.createSceneObject(name)
38	    root.setParent(parent)
39	    const mat = this.makeMaterial(color, true)
40	    for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
41	      const bar = global.scene.createSceneObject("Edge" + i)
42	      bar.setParent(root)
43	      const rmv = bar.createComponent("Component.RenderMeshVisual") as RenderMeshVisual
44	      rmv.mesh = this.mesh
45	      rmv.mainMaterial = mat
46	    }
47	    BoxFactory.layoutWireBox(root, size, thickness)
48	    return root
49	  }
50	
51	  static layoutWireBox(root: SceneObject, size: vec3, th: number): void {
52	    const hx = size.x / 2, hy = size.y / 2, hz = size.z / 2
53	    const specs: [vec3, vec3][] = []
54	    for (const sy of [-1, 1]) for (const sz of [-1, 1]) specs.push([new vec3(0, sy * hy, sz * hz), new vec3(size.x + th, th, th)])
55	    for (const sx of [-1, 1]) for (const sz of [-1, 1]) specs.push([new vec3(sx * hx, 0, sz * hz), new vec3(th, size.y + th, th)])
56	    for (const sx of [-1, 1]) for (const sy of [-1, 1]) specs.push([new vec3(sx * hx, sy * hy, 0), new vec3(th, th, size.z + th)])
57	    for (let i = 0; i < 12 && i < root.getChildrenCount(); i++) {
58	      const t = root.getChild(i).getTransform()
59	      t.setLocalPosition(specs[i][0])
60	      t.setLocalScale(specs[i][1])
61	    }
62	  }
63	}

#!/bin/sh
# Session 6 (2026-11-09): wrap the red tip so it fits the view, add a scripted "demo" driver mode
# that plays a full order like a person would, and screen-record it from the preview for the video.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." || exit 1
claude -p "$(cat <<'EOF'
Lens Studio is open with this project (Stack Right; devpost/design-brief.md is the approved brief). Work through the CLAD skills and the Lens Studio MCP. Bash and ffmpeg (C:/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe) are available.

Goal: a clean screen recording of the Lens being played, for a demo video under 3 minutes. Do these in order.

1. Tip fits the view. The red tip ("That leaves a gap. Drop it on the ghost.") is currently one line wider than the view and gets cut off at both sides. Make every tip and the layer-done note break into two lines at the sentence break (". " -> ".\n"), and make sure the text block is no wider than the pallet (116.5 cm) when seen from the default position. Keep the size readable. Update any test that checks the exact tip string (the controller's getTipText or similar; LEAF scenarios in Assets/Tests and their copies in devpost/leaf-scenarios).

2. Demo mode. Add mode "demo" to Assets/Scripts/StackRightTestDriver.ts (next to the existing "paced" mode). It plays the whole order through the controller's existing grab/release hooks, but the held case visibly travels from its pick-face slot to the drop point along a smooth arc (ease in/out, lifted about 30 cm above the stack top) while it is held, so the ghost is visible during the carry. Script, with a log line "[DEMO] <beat>" at the start of each beat:
   - intro: 4 s idle on the start layout.
   - case1: slow carry (3 s), hover 1.5 s right above the ghost so the tag can be read, drop -> snap. Pause 1.5 s.
   - overhang: case 2 carried to a spot where it hangs about 15 cm over the pallet's side edge, drop -> red overhang tip, slides back. Pause 3.5 s.
   - gap: case 2 dropped on the pallet but clearly away from its slot -> red gap tip, slides back. Pause 3.5 s.
   - case2: case 2 carried to its ghost and placed (2 s carry).
   - layer1: rest of layer 1 at 1.4 s per case. Hold on the layer-done note 3.5 s.
   - layer2turn: first case of layer 2 slowly (3 s carry, 1.5 s hover) so the turned ghost is obvious, then the rest of layer 2 at 0.9 s per case.
   - fast: layers 3 and 4 at 0.5 s per case (the video will also speed this up).
   - layer5: layer 5 at 1.4 s per case.
   - complete: hold on the completion card 7 s.
   - reset: press Reset, hold 3 s.
   - end.
   The demo mode must not change any game rule; it only drives the hooks and moves the held case. Leave the default driver mode "off" when you finish.

3. Framing. The video needs a 16:9 landscape view that shows the pallet, the pick face and the ghost tag at the same time, and later the completion card at the top of the stack. Make the Preview panel as large and landscape as Lens Studio allows (maximize/undock it; set a 16:9 preview resolution such as 1920x1080 if the option exists). Pick a viewpoint a person could plausibly stand at (eye height about 165 cm, a step back and to the left of the default so both pallet and shelf are in frame). If the demo mode can set the camera transform in the preview without fighting device tracking, do it there (and restore the default camera behaviour outside demo mode); otherwise position the preview camera with the Interactive Preview controls before recording. Take a CapturePanelScreenshotTool screenshot of the framing and check by eye that pallet, shelf, tag and the 180 cm line are all in frame before recording.

4. Record. Start ffmpeg in the background capturing the screen region of the Preview panel only (gdigrab, -framerate 30, offset/size of the panel, or the whole window then crop), x264 crf 18, to devpost/video/raw_demo.mp4. Write the wall-clock time ffmpeg started (with milliseconds) to devpost/video/record_start.txt. Then switch the driver to demo mode and restart the preview, wait until the "[DEMO] end" log line (or 4 minutes max), then stop ffmpeg cleanly (send q). Copy every "[DEMO]" and "[StackRight]" log line with its timestamp into devpost/video/demo_beats.log. Afterwards set the driver mode back to "off" and save the scene.

5. Check the recording: extract frames at the case1 hover, the overhang tip, the gap tip, the layer2turn hover and the completion card (ffmpeg -ss using the beat times relative to record_start) into devpost/video/check-*.png, look at each one, and report honestly whether each shows what it should (text readable, nothing cut off). If something important is out of frame or unreadable, fix the framing and record again (at most 2 more attempts).

6. Re-run the self-test and the LEAF scenarios after the tip change; append results to devpost/selftest-2026-11-09.log.

Known gotchas on this machine: injected mouse input does not register grabs in the preview, so don't rely on it. CaptureRuntimeViewTool and the preview-interaction package install can freeze Lens Studio or break the compile, so avoid them. Open pop-ups silently block the TypeScript compiler; if compiles stop reporting, say so instead of looping. Don't create material assets without a shader. Don't touch .agents/skills, .claude/skills or Plugins/. Keep everything bright on the additive display; units are cm.

Do not git commit, push, or touch anything outside this project folder. When done, print a short report: the tip change, the demo beats with their times relative to the recording start, the recording's path, length and resolution, what each check frame showed, test totals, and anything unfinished.
EOF

  > devpost/agent-logs/06-demo-v4.jsonl 2> devpost/agent-logs/06-demo-v4.err
echo "exit $?"

304	  const so = findSceneObjectByName("StackRightController")

311	/** World point from Pallet-local cm (x right, y up from the floor, z toward the user). */
312	export function palletPoint(c: StackRightController, x: number, y: number, z: number): vec3 {
313	  return c.getPalletWorldTransform().multiplyPoint(new vec3(x, y, z))
314	}
315	
316	/** Grabs case i and drops it a few cm above its slot (inside the 15 cm snap radius). */
317	export function dropOnSlot(c: StackRightController, i: number): void {
318	  c.simulateGrab(i)
319	  c.simulateRelease(i, c.getSlotWorldPosition(i).add(new vec3(0, 5, 0)))
320	}

323	export function dropAt(c: StackRightController, i: number, x: number, y: number, z: number): void {

325	  c.simulateRelease(i, palletPoint(c, x, y, z))
326	}

332	    for (let i = 0; i < c.getCaseCount(); i++) if (c.isCaseReturning(i)) busy = true
333	    if (!busy) return
334	    await sleep(100)
335	  }
336	}

343	/** Angle in degrees between two rotations. */
344	export function angleDeg(a: quat, b: quat): number {
345	  const d = Math.min(1, Math.abs(a.w * b.w + a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z))
346	  return (2 * Math.acos(d) * 180) / Math.PI
347	}

351	  const next = c.getNextIndex()
352	  for (let i = 0; i < c.getCaseCount(); i++) {
353	    const inQueue = i >= next && i < next + c.getQueueSize()
354	    if (c.isCaseShown(i) !== (inQueue || c.isCasePlaced(i))) return false

<!--

-->

# Lens Studio Router

This skill prepares the Lens Studio environment and routes the request to the right platform workflow: **Detect → Gate → Route → Post-build**. **You** (the main agent loading this skill) execute every step inline — running this orchestration as a skill keeps subagent spawns at depth 1, where they actually fire (a sub-agent's nested `Agent` calls are silently no-op'd by default; do not refactor this back into a sub-agent). You do not build anything yourself: for Specs you spawn `specs-experience-builder`; for Snapchat you continue inline using core Lens Studio skills.

## Cross-runtime behavior (read first)

This skill ships to Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex from one file. The canonical semantics live in `lens-studio-field-notes` — tool naming: Hard Rule 2; ask/spawn/skill-invoke: Cross-runtime orchestration. Entry-point summary, applied by **intent**, never by the literal tool name:

- **Asking the user.** Present the question as a *blocking* choice using your runtime's ask facility and wait for the answer — Claude Code: `AskUserQuestion` (blocking); Cursor: its ask tool, which is **non-blocking**, so end your turn and wait for the user yourself (it does not recognize the literal symbol `AskUserQuestion`); Codex: an ask tool exists in **Plan mode only** (`codex exec` is fully non-interactive). Print a blocked payload **only when no human can answer in this run at all**. The literal `AskUserQuestion` symbol being absent is **not** "no human can answer": Cursor and Codex Plan-mode can still ask, and reading it that way wrongly skips the platform and sign-in gates.

- **Spawning subagents** (builder, tester). "Spawn X" means: if your runtime can spawn a subagent, do so — Claude Code: `Agent({ subagent_type: "ls-clad:X" })` (plugin-qualified; the bare name fails to resolve — copy the qualified name from the error's "Available agents:" list if you see one); Cursor: its own subagent facility. **If your runtime cannot spawn a markdown subagent at all** — Codex's agents are TOML, so it never loads `ls-clad/agents/*.md` — that is **not** a missing install: load the named agent's file (`ls-clad/agents/X.md`) and execute its procedure **inline** in this same context. Only treat a spawn failure as a missing/partial install when the agent's source file is genuinely absent.

## Product naming

**Specs** is the current product name for Snap's AR glasses; **Spectacles** is the former name for the same device — treat them as synonyms and prefer "Specs" in everything you say back to the user. This is a naming convention only — it does **not** rename code identifiers (`SpectaclesInteractionKit`, `SpectaclesUIKit`, `SpectaclesSyncKit`), the `Editor.TargetPlatform.Spectacles` enum value, package names like `Spectacles 3D Hand Hints`, or historical references such as "Spectacles (2024)" (the prior hardware generation). When the platform question is asked, display the AR-glasses option as **SPECS** ("Lightweight AR glasses") and the camera option as **Snapchat**; record the canonical values `Specs` / `Snapchat` for routing and the `platform:` payload field.

## Modes

- **`mode: full`** (default) — Detect → Gate → Route, then Post-build for Specs.
- **`mode: preflight_only`** — Detect + Gate only, then print the preflight-ready payload (Route's preflight branch). No platform resolution, no routing, no post-build. For callers that need to verify Lens Studio is open, MCP is up, and the user is signed in — without triggering a full build. Requires an existing project at cwd (no `.esproj` → blocked payload `reason: no_project_present`). Failures print the same blocked payloads as `full` mode.

Anything other than an explicit `mode: preflight_only` — including ambiguous input — is treated as `full`.

## Hard rules

- **Do NOT build inline.** This skill only prepares the environment and routes the request.
- **Specs path:** spawn the `specs-experience-builder` sub-agent (see Cross-runtime behavior, including the inline-degrade path) with the HANDOFF_PAYLOAD as its prompt. That agent runs the whole build in its own context. Do not spawn `script-author` or other build agents from this skill.
- **Snapchat path:** print the handoff payload and continue inline. There is no dedicated Snapchat orchestrator yet.
- **Do NOT use `curl`, `fetch`, `wget`, or raw HTTP** to the Lens Studio MCP server as a workaround for MCP failures. If MCP is not reachable through tools, classify the blocker (see `references/environment-edge-cases.md`) and report a blocked payload.
- **Platform precedence: user-stated → project-stated → ask. Never guess.** A platform the user named is final. Otherwise the open project's `.esproj` `targetPlatform` decides, announced with a one-line override. Ask only when both are silent or ambiguous (details in Route).
- **Do NOT re-open a project that is already loaded.** Probe MCP and compare the loaded project against `project_path` before any `open -a`. On mismatch, ask before switching — never auto-switch an unrelated session.
- **Sign-in gate is mandatory and default-deny.** Check `isAuthorized` exactly once; only an explicit `true` proceeds. Never call `Editor.IAuthorization.authorize()` and never poll `isAuthorized` in a loop — ask once, re-check once.
- Tool naming, deferred-schema handling (`InputValidationError` = schema not loaded, NOT tool missing), and ask/spawn semantics: see `lens-studio-field-notes` Hard Rule 2 / Cross-runtime orchestration.

## Detect — find the project

The cwd is a Lens Studio project if **either** holds:

1. A `*.esproj` file exists at the cwd root (strongest signal — every LS project has exactly one).
2. `Assets/` AND `Packages/` directories exist together at cwd.

```bash
ls *.esproj 2>/dev/null | head -1
test -d Assets && test -d Packages && echo "ASSETS_AND_PACKAGES_PRESENT"
```

- **Project found** → record `project_path` (absolute path to the `.esproj`) and proceed to Gate.
- **No project found** (either mode) → this skill does **not** scaffold a project. Print a blocked payload with `reason: no_project_present` and stop, with `suggested_next_step`: open Lens Studio with the intended project, then fully restart the coding-assistant session so it re-registers the Lens Studio MCP server at startup, then re-invoke this skill (or, in preflight mode, the skill that triggered the preflight) from that project's directory. The MCP endpoint is registered at session start — no project at startup means the Lens Studio MCP tools are absent for the whole session, and only a restart recovers them.

## Gate — Lens Studio readiness

Lens Studio configures and owns the MCP endpoint; this skill owns only the generic app/project/MCP/sign-in gate. Platform-specific setup (Blender, Node.js, SIK/UIKit, preview device, scene bootstrap) belongs to the routed workflow. **Required version: Lens Studio 5.22 or higher** — versions below 5.22, and dev builds whose version is unreadable, are incompatible.

**Preload (Claude Code only).** Resolve the two deferred MCP tool schemas before any MCP call — skipping this is the #1 cause of the sign-in gate silently failing, because the first `ExecuteEditorCode` call returns `InputValidationError`, which is "schema not loaded", NOT "tool missing" (see `lens-studio-field-notes` Hard Rule 2):

```text
ToolSearch({ query: "select:mcp__lens-studio__ListAllPanels", max_results: 1 })
ToolSearch({ query: "select:mcp__lens-studio__ExecuteEditorCode", max_results: 1 })
```

Codex/Cursor surface `ListAllPanels` and `ExecuteEditorCode` directly — skip the preload. If either fails to resolve on Claude Code, the MCP server was not registered with this agent at startup: print blocked payload `reason: mcp_plugin_off` and stop — do not attempt MCP calls without a resolved schema.

**Probe.** Call the `ListAllPanels` MCP tool once.

- **Probe succeeds** → MCP is reachable; some project is loaded. Read which one via `ExecuteEditorCode`:

  ```ts
  const model = pluginSystem.findInterface(Editor.Model.IModel);
  return model.project.projectFile.toString();
  ```

  Normalize both paths (trim whitespace, strip trailing `/`, resolve `..`; macOS paths are case-sensitive — compare exactly) and compare against `project_path`.
  - **Match** → tell the user the project is already open (skip re-open), set `mcp_status: ready`, and continue to the sign-in check.
  - **Mismatch** → ask (blocking): *"Lens Studio currently has `<current_project>` open. Switch to `<project_path>`?"* — **Switch** → `open -a "<lens_studio_path>" "<project_path>"`, then wait for MCP on the new project per `references/environment-edge-cases.md`; **Cancel**, or no human can answer in this run → blocked payload `reason: wrong_project_open`. Never auto-switch.
  - **`ExecuteEditorCode` fails despite the successful probe** (rare) → treat as Mismatch with `<current_project>` = "unknown".

- **Probe fails** → Lens Studio may not be running, may have no project loaded, may have its MCP plugin off, or there may be multiple/incompatible installs to sort out. **Read `references/environment-edge-cases.md` now** and follow it: compatible-install detection and version partition (5.22+), the multi-install picker, launch + the bounded MCP wait, and failure classification into the blocked-payload taxonomy.

**Sign-in check (mandatory, default-deny).** After MCP is confirmed, verify the user is signed in to Lens Studio (`Editor.IAuthorization` — the account login that gates publishing, asset-library access, and account-bound APIs). MCP being reachable does NOT imply sign-in. Check once via `ExecuteEditorCode`:

```ts
try {
  const auth = pluginSystem.findInterface(Editor.IAuthorization);
  if (!auth) return { isAuthorized: null, error: "no_auth_interface" };
  return { isAuthorized: auth.isAuthorized };
} catch (e) {
  return { isAuthorized: null, error: String(e) };
}
```

**Only `isAuthorized === true` proceeds to Route.** Anything else — `false`, `null`, `undefined`, missing field, thrown error, unrecognized shape, or `InputValidationError` (re-run the preload and retry the call once before treating it as fatal) — is "not signed in". Then:

1. Tell the user in plain text: *"You're not signed in to Lens Studio. Open the Lens Studio profile menu (top-right of the toolbar) and sign in."* **Account-agnostic copy is mandatory** — never name a specific account, email, username, or login provider, and never inject a development-time identity (shell email, git config) into the prompt. The user chooses the account.
2. Ask (blocking): *"Have you signed in to Lens Studio?"* — **I've signed in** / **Cancel**.
3. **I've signed in** → re-check `isAuthorized` with one more `ExecuteEditorCode` call (same snippet). `true` → continue to Route. Anything else → blocked payload `reason: not_signed_in`; do not re-prompt — re-invocation is cleaner than nested asks. If the re-check call itself fails, treat as `mcp_down`.
4. **Cancel**, or no human can answer in this run → blocked payload `reason: not_signed_in`. Never poll as a fallback — signing in is a human action with no upper bound.

Do not call `auth.authorize()` from this skill — sign-in must be user-initiated from the Lens Studio UI.

## Route — resolve platform, hand off

**If `mode: preflight_only`, skip platform resolution entirely** — print the preflight payload below and stop.

### Resolve the platform

Precedence: **user-stated → project-stated → ask. Never guess.**

1. **User stated it.** Scan `original_request` for an explicit platform name (apply Product-naming synonyms): Specs / Spectacles / "Snap('s) AR glasses" / "(on / for) my glasses" → **Specs**; Snapchat / "Snap camera" / "a Snapchat Lens" → **Snapchat**. Exactly one named → that is `platform`; route directly with one line: *"Building for `<platform>` (you said so)."* Generic terms — "Lens", "AR", "3D game", "app", "experience", "prototype" — are **not** a platform statement; both platforms have them.
2. **Project states it.** Otherwise, read the open project's `.esproj` and check its `targetPlatform` field. If it names exactly one platform (`Spectacles` → Specs, `Snapchat` → Snapchat), route on it and announce with a one-line override — e.g. *"Building for Specs — project targets Spectacles; say 'Snapchat' to switch."* A user-stated platform always wins over the project file.
3. **Ask** — only when the user didn't state it AND the `.esproj` field is absent, names both platforms, or is otherwise ambiguous. Ask (blocking): *"Which platform are you building for?"* — options **SPECS** (description leads with "Lightweight AR glasses") / **Snapchat**. Normalize the answer to canonical `Specs` / `Snapchat`. If no human can answer in this run, print blocked payload `reason: platform_choice_required` — do not pick a platform by guessing from genre or phrasing.

Auto / "don't ask me" directives don't change this: steps 1–2 already avoid the question in most runs; when both are silent, the question is still required (there is no build without a platform).

### Handoff payload

```
HANDOFF_PAYLOAD
- platform: <Specs | Snapchat>
- project_path: <absolute path to .esproj>
- project_state: existing
- lens_studio_path: <chosen Lens Studio app bundle>
- lens_studio_version: <5.22 or higher>
- mcp_status: <ready | not-ready>
- original_request: <the user's most recent pre-skill request, verbatim>
```

### If mode == preflight_only

Print this payload and stop — do NOT spawn the builder, ask the platform, or print next-step suggestions. The caller resumes its own work.

```
HANDOFF_PAYLOAD
- mode: preflight_only
- status: ready
- project_path: <absolute path to .esproj>
- project_state: existing
- lens_studio_path: <chosen Lens Studio app bundle>
- lens_studio_version: <5.22 or higher>
- mcp_status: ready
- is_authorized: true
- original_request: <the caller's original_request, verbatim>
```

### If platform == Specs

Spawn the builder — plugin-qualified `ls-clad:specs-experience-builder` (see Cross-runtime behavior; on a runtime that can't spawn subagents, load `ls-clad/agents/specs-experience-builder.md` and run its pipeline inline, in which case Post-build below is also yours to run directly) — with this prompt:

```
HANDOFF_PAYLOAD
- platform: Specs
- project_path: <absolute path to .esproj>
- project_state: existing
- lens_studio_path: <chosen Lens Studio app bundle>
- lens_studio_version: <5.22 or higher>
- mcp_status: ready
- original_request: <the user's most recent pre-skill request, verbatim>

You are continuing a Lens Studio request after environment routing. Treat this handoff as authoritative.

Proceed as the Specs Experience Builder:
- Print the HANDOFF_PAYLOAD verbatim first so the relevant facts are anchored for compaction.
- Satisfy `original_request`.
- Follow your pipeline (sequential build — assets via /build-mesh, /build-sfx, /build-music, /specs-build-ui, /icon-selector, then scripts, then bootstrap).
```

When the builder returns, parse its return text for the machine-readable summary block (a fenced ```yaml block under `### Machine-readable summary (for router/verifier)`), surface the human-readable report to the user, and continue to Post-build. If the builder returned a blocked / error result (no machine-readable summary, build failed), surface its result as-is and stop — no post-build step on a failed build.

### If platform == Snapchat

Print the HANDOFF_PAYLOAD (platform: Snapchat), then continue inline:

1. One short message: "Continuing on the Snapchat-camera path. There's no dedicated orchestrator yet — using core Lens Studio skills directly."
2. **Mandatory: invoke the `lens-studio-field-notes` skill now, before any other LS work in this session.** It carries the scene/asset tool-selection rules (VirtualScene-first), the GraphQL call recipes, and the domain-skill index that prevent the most common failures. Do NOT defer it until something fails.
3. **Mandatory before any `ExecuteEditorCode` call: load the `ls-clad:editor-api` skill** (or delegate the work to the `editor-api-specialist` subagent, which auto-loads it). It carries the `findInterface` namespace rules and the `editor.d.ts` lookup workflow — do NOT write Editor API code from memory.
4. Surface these other core skills with one-liners: /lens-api, /scene-construction (covers scene-graphql + asset-graphql via its references/), /materials, /camera-and-rendering, /lens-log-analysis.
5. Ask the user what they want to build next, then continue inline using the listed skills.

The Snapchat path is one-shot — it ends here; Post-build is Specs-only today.

## Post-build (Specs only)

After surfacing the builder's report, verify the build per `lens-studio-field-notes` → **See-and-fix loop** — recompile, log-diff, capture the preview, and judge the capture yourself with full code context, inline in the main agent (the `ls-clad:verify-preview` skill is the Lens-specific QA pass). Then print this plain-text suggestion and end the turn:

```

1. Grep for `class MeshBuilder` in `Support/StudioLib.d.ts` and read the full class definition for exact method signatures.

   | Shape | Generator | Reference |
   |---|---|---|
   | Rotationally symmetric (chess piece, vase, map pin) | **lathe** | `smooth-surfaces.md` |
   | 2D outline with depth (heart, star, coin, gear) | **extrude** | `smooth-surfaces.md` |
   | Circular cross-section swept along a path (pipe, cable) | **tube** | `smooth-surfaces.md` |
   | Angular / modular / blocky (crates, walls, pixel-art) | stack `addBox`/`buildCylinder` | `primitives.md` |

     ```ts

      )

      }
      ```

{ name: "color",     components: 4 }           // include by default (RGBA, per-vertex)

# MeshBuilder API (Runtime)

## API Reference

The core classes live in `Support/StudioLib.d.ts`. Grep for each symbol by name to find the current definition:

| Symbol | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `MeshBuilder` | Construct and mutate meshes at runtime |
| `MeshTopology` | Topology enum (Triangles, TriangleStrip, TriangleFan, Points, Lines, LineStrip) |
| `MeshIndexType` | Index type enum (None, UInt16) |

Grep for `class MeshBuilder`, `enum MeshTopology`, and `enum MeshIndexType` in `StudioLib.d.ts` to get the current method signatures (`appendVerticesInterleaved`, `setVertexInterleaved`, `appendIndices`, `eraseVertices`, `eraseIndices`, `getMesh`, `updateMesh`, `setBones`, etc.). This is the same discipline as `lens-studio-field-notes` "Verify the API surface before writing" — apply it to any other unfamiliar LS API too.

## Resources

This skill includes a pre-built vertex color package:

```
{skill_base_dir}/resources/SimpleVertexBaseColor.lspkg
```

Contains `vertexBaseColorMaterial` (UUID: `70d03593-c7b4-410a-ae5c-75cb82ee32dc`) — purpose-built for per-vertex color rendering. Use this instead of UberPBR.

### Material Do / Don't

- **Do** import the packaged `SimpleVertexBaseColor.lspkg` and wire `vertexBaseColorMaterial` (UUID above) to the script's `@input material`. This is the default path.
- **Do** alternatively use Uber PBR / UberUnlit with `passInfos.0.Vertex Color` set to `"Base Color"` (`valueType: STRING`) if you need PBR shading on top of vertex colors.
- **Do** query `asset-graphql assetsByName(name: "vertexBaseColorMaterial")` first if you're not sure whether the package is already installed — avoid re-importing.
- **Don't** hand-write `.mat` YAML files. The UUIDs can collide with Lens Studio built-ins silently (producing "Duplicate material id" warnings and leaving `this.material` null at runtime), and `PassesInfo` is non-trivial to construct correctly.
- **Don't** create a material without a shader assigned — an empty `PassesInfo: []` will load but render as null.

1. Grep for `class MeshBuilder` in `Support/StudioLib.d.ts` and read the full class definition for exact method signatures.

   |---|---|---|
   | Rotationally symmetric (chess piece, vase, map pin) | **lathe** | `smooth-surfaces.md` |

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent (the user's one message, the same text as the prompt in devpost/agent-logs/run_shapes_v6.sh):
   Lens Studio project "Stack Right" (pallet-building trainer for Specs). Make the order realistic without breaking any existing rule, interaction, the ghost/tag/snap/tip/card behaviour, the demo driver or the tests. Work through the CLAD skills and the Lens Studio MCP; Bash and ffmpeg (C:/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe) are available.

   1. **New ORDER_LINES.** Still heaviest first. Sizes are W x D x H in cm. Every case in a layer has the same H.
      - L1: PET FOOD 20kg, 20 kg, 55x37x14, count 6, sack.
      - L2: LAUNDRY 4x4L, 17 kg, 38x58x30, count 6, carton.
      - L3 (mixed, turned 90): WATER 24, 14 kg, 38x58x25, count 4, carton; JUICE 12x1L, 12 kg, 38x29x25, count 4, carton.
      - L4: TINNED TOMATOES 2x24, 10 kg, 57x38x13, count 6, tray (spec says 2 per row, 3 rows).
      - L5 (mixed, fragile on top):
        - BREAD, 4 kg, 56x45x30, count 2, fragile.
        - PAPER TOWEL 12, 3 kg, 112x25x30, count 1, "long" carton.
        - CHIPS, 2 kg, 56x45x30, count 2, fragile.
      - Totals: 31 cases; height 15 + 14+30+25+13+30 = 127 cm. Colours bright and light (additive display).
   2. **Computed plan with row (shelf) packing.**
      - Per-line or per-layer turned flag instead of TURNED_LAYERS.
      - Fill each row left to right while it fits 116.5 cm; start a new row nearer the user when it doesn't.
      - Row depth = deepest case in the row. Centre each row in x and the whole layer in z.
      - Print an error on overflow or mixed heights.
      - Check that each layer's joints cross the layer below and say so in the report.
      - Layer-done notes are per layer, two lines, and must be true for the plan. Examples: "Layer 2 done.\nNext layer turns 90° so the joints cross." and "Layer 3 done.\nFlat trays next: keep the top level."
   3. **Shapes from primitives/MeshBuilder.** No new material assets without a shader; reuse the BoxFactory/material-clone pattern.
      - sack: soft, rounded pillow, must not read as a cube.
      - tray: about 4 cm cardboard lip, tins as a grid of short cylinders, faint clear shrink-wrap box.
      - long: an ordinary carton 112 cm long.
      - carton: as now.
      - Labels (name + kg + HEAVY/FRAGILE) readable on every shape.
      - Ghost = wire bounding box; colliders = bounding box.
      - Cases must not poke through the shelf uprights. Widen the shelf or queue spacing if needed, keeping it 1.4 m to the right.

      - Two forks visible in the pallet openings.
      - Power unit about 80x60x120, bright safety yellow/orange, on a side that doesn't block the pallet, pick face or ghost.
      - Operator platform and tiller.

273	  /** All cases of the order, under PickList: authored children are reused, the rest created. */
274	  private buildCases(): void {
275	    for (let i = 0; i < ORDER.length; i++) {
276	      const spec = ORDER[i]
277	      let so: SceneObject
278	      if (i < this.pickList.getChildrenCount()) {
279	        so = this.pickList.getChild(i)
280	      } else {
281	        so = global.scene.createSceneObject("Case")
282	        so.setParent(this.pickList)
283	      }
284	      so.name = "Case_" + (i < 10 ? "0" : "") + i + "_" + spec.key
285	      // Neighbouring cases in a layer alternate between two shades so the joints read clearly.
286	      const slot = PLAN[i]
287	      const k = (slot.row + slot.col) % 2 === 0 ? 0 : 0.3
288	      const bodyColor = new vec4(spec.color.x + (1 - spec.color.x) * k, spec.color.y + (1 - spec.color.y) * k,
289	        spec.color.z + (1 - spec.color.z) * k, 1)
290	      const body = this.factory.makeBox(so, "Body", spec.size, vec3.zero(), bodyColor)
291	      const glowRmv = this.factory.makeBox(so, "Glow", spec.size.add(new vec3(5, 5, 5)), vec3.zero(), this.glowColor, true)
292	      const labels = so.createComponent(StackRightCartonLabelUI.getTypeName()) as StackRightCartonLabelUI
293	      labels.setup(spec.name, spec.kg + " kg · " + (spec.fragile ? "FRAGILE" : "HEAVY"), spec.size)
294	
295	      const col = so.createComponent("Physics.ColliderComponent") as ColliderComponent
296	      const shape = Shape.createBoxShape()
297	      shape.size = spec.size
298	      col.shape = shape
299	      const interactable = so.createComponent(Interactable.getTypeName()) as Interactable
300	      const manip = so.createComponent(InteractableManipulation.getTypeName()) as InteractableManipulation
301	      manip.setCanRotate(false)
302	      manip.setCanScale(false)
303	
304	      this.cases.push({
305	        index: i, spec, so,
306	        home: so.getTransform().getWorldPosition(),
307	        placed: false, grabbed: false, returning: false, returnFrom: vec3.zero(), returnT: 0, hovered: false,
308	        interactable, manip,
309	        bodyMat: body.mainMaterial,
310	        bodyColor,
311	        glow: glowRmv.getSceneObject(),
312	        glowMat: glowRmv.mainMaterial,
313	      })
314	    }
315	    for (let k = ORDER.length; k < this.pickList.getChildrenCount(); k++) this.pickList.getChild(k).enabled = false
316	  }

318	  private buildAudio(): void {
319	    const tracks: {[k: string]: AudioTrackAsset} = {chime: SFX_CHIME, snap: SFX_SNAP, mistake: SFX_MISTAKE, complete: SFX_COMPLETE}
320	    for (const k of Object.keys(tracks)) {
321	      const so = global.scene.createSceneObject("Sfx_" + k)
322	      so.setParent(this.sceneObject)
323	      const a = so.createComponent("Component.AudioComponent") as AudioComponent
324	      a.audioTrack = tracks[k]
325	      a.playbackMode = Audio.PlaybackMode.LowLatency
326	      a.volume = 0.8
327	      this.audio[k] = a
328	    }
329	  }
330	
331	  private play(k: string): void {
332	    const a = this.audio[k]
333	    if (!a) return
334	    if (a.isPlaying()) a.stop(false)
335	    a.play(1)
336	  }

339	    if (this.debugLogs) print("[StackRight] " + msg)
340	  }

342	  private validateRefs(): boolean {
343	    const missing: string[] = []
344	    const refs: {[k: string]: any} = {
345	      pallet: this.pallet, shelfBay: this.shelfBay, pickList: this.pickList, ghost: this.ghost,
346	      offViewArrow: this.offViewArrow, resetPost: this.resetPost, ghostTag: this.ghostTag, counter: this.counter,
347	      tipText: this.tipText, completionCard: this.completionCard, resetButton: this.resetButton,
348	      boxMesh: this.boxMesh, baseMaterial: this.baseMaterial,
349	    }
350	    for (const k of Object.keys(refs)) if (isNull(refs[k])) missing.push(k)
351	    if (missing.length > 0) {
352	      print("[StackRight] ERROR: unwired @input(s): " + missing.join(", "))
353	      return false
354	    }
355	    return true
356	  }

178	      if (c.isCasePlaced(i)) continue
179	      const q = i - next
180	      const inQueue = q >= 0 && q < c.getQueueSize()
181	      if (c.isCaseShown(i) !== inQueue) return false
182	      if (inQueue && c.getCaseHomePosition(i).distance(c.getQueueSlotWorldPosition(q, i)) > 0.5) return false
183	    }
184	    return true
185	  }
186	
187	  private onlyInteractable(i: number): boolean {
188	    const c = this.controller
189	    for (let k = 0; k < c.getCaseCount(); k++) if (c.isCaseInteractable(k) !== (k === i)) return false
190	    return true
191	  }
192	
193	  /** Prints which joint lines (cm, pallet axes) each pair of neighbouring layers share. */
194	  private logJoints(): void {
195	    const joints = (layer: number, axis: "x" | "z"): number[] => {
196	      const out: number[] = []
197	      for (let i = 0; i < PLAN.length; i++) {
198	        if (PLAN[i].layer !== layer) continue
199	        const fp = footprint(ORDER[i], PLAN[i].turned)
200	        const half = axis === "x" ? fp.x / 2 : fp.y / 2
201	        const ctr = axis === "x" ? PLAN[i].center.x : PLAN[i].center.z
202	        for (const e of [ctr - half, ctr + half]) {
203	          const r = Math.round(e * 10) / 10
204	          if (Math.abs(r) < 55 && out.indexOf(r) < 0) out.push(r)
205	        }
206	      }
207	      return out.sort((a, b) => a - b)
208	    }
209	    for (let l = 1; l < LAYER_COUNT; l++) {
210	      const shared: string[] = []
211	      for (const axis of ["x", "z"] as ("x" | "z")[]) {
212	        const lo = joints(l, axis), hi = joints(l + 1, axis)
213	        for (const j of lo) if (hi.indexOf(j) >= 0) shared.push(axis + "=" + j)
214	      }
215	      print("[StackRightTest] INFO joints shared by layers " + l + " and " + (l + 1) + ": " + (shared.length ? shared.join(", ") : "none"))
216	    }
217	  }
218	
219	  private palletPoint(x: number, y: number, z: number): vec3 {
220	    return this.controller.getPalletWorldTransform().multiplyPoint(new vec3(x, y, z))
221	  }
222	
223	  private dropOnSlot(i: number): void {
224	    this.controller.simulateGrab(i)
225	    this.controller.simulateRelease(i, this.controller.getSlotWorldPosition(i).add(new vec3(0, 5, 0)))
226	  }
227	
228	  private flatDist(a: vec3, b: vec3): number {
229	    return Math.sqrt((a.x - b.x) * (a.x - b.x) + (a.z - b.z) * (a.z - b.z))
230	  }
231	
232	  private angleDeg(a: quat, b: quat): number {
233	    const d = Math.abs(a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z + a.w * b.w)
234	    return 2 * Math.acos(Math.min(1, d)) * 180 / Math.PI
235	  }
236	
237	  private v(p: vec3): string {
238	    return "(" + p.x.toFixed(0) + ", " + p.y.toFixed(0) + ", " + p.z.toFixed(0) + ")"
239	  }
240	
241	  private check(dc: string, what: string, ok: boolean): void {
242	    if (ok) this.passed++
243	    else this.failed++
244	    const r = this.dcResults[dc] || [0, 0]
245	    r[ok ? 0 : 1]++
246	    this.dcResults[dc] = r
247	    print("[StackRightTest] " + (ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL") + " " + dc + ": " + what)
248	  }
249	
250	  private async settle(): Promise<void> {
251	    for (let k = 0; k < 30; k++) {
252	      let busy = false
253	      for (let i = 0; i < this.controller.getCaseCount(); i++) if (this.controller.isCaseReturning(i)) busy = true
254	      if (!busy) return
255	      await this.wait(0.1)
256	    }
257	  }
258	
259	  private wait(sec: number): Promise<void> {
260	    return new Promise((resolve) => {
261	      const ev = this.createEvent("DelayedCallbackEvent")
262	      ev.bind(() => resolve())
263	      ev.reset(sec)
264	    })
265	  }
266	}

#!/bin/sh
# usage: record.sh <scratch dir>; records the Preview region until "[DEMO] end" appears in the LS log after start.
S="$1"; V=/c/Users/Fatal/Desktop/specs_hackathon/pallet_lens/devpost/video
L="C:/Users/Fatal/AppData/Local/Snap/Lens Studio/logs/LensStudioLog-2026-11-08-22-37-48-770-b5e8c.txt"
OFF=$(stat -c %s "$L"); echo "$OFF" > "$S/log_offset.txt"; rm -f "$S/stop.flag"
date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N" > $V/record_start.txt
{ while [ ! -f "$S/stop.flag" ]; do sleep 0.1; done; printf q; sleep 6; } | \
  /c/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe -y -f gdigrab -framerate 30 -offset_x 2292 -offset_y 87 -video_size 1476x830 -draw_mouse 0 -i desktop -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p $V/raw_demo.mp4 > "$S/ffmpeg.log" 2>&1 &
i=0
while [ $i -lt 1500 ]; do   # 5 min cap at 0.2 s
  if tail -c +$((OFF+1)) "$L" | grep -aq "\[DEMO\] end"; then break; fi
  sleep 0.2; i=$((i+1))
done
date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N" > "$S/stop_time.txt"; touch "$S/stop.flag"; wait
echo "ffmpeg exited"; tail -c 300 "$S/ffmpeg.log"

content.content: 1 // StackRightCartonLabelUI.ts 2 // Owns: the printed labels on one carton (name + "14 kg · HEAVY" / "FRAGILE") on the faces the 3 // user sees: the side facing the pallet (-X, seen while the carton is on the shelf), the near 4 // side (+Z, seen on the pallet) and the top. Created at runtime by the controller on each carton. 5 // Must not: hold game state. 6 7 @component 8 export class StackRightCartonLabelUI extends BaseScriptComponent { 9 @ui.label('StackRightCartonLabelUI – printed carton labels') 10 @ui.separator 11 12 @ui.label('Settings') 13 @ui.group_start("Settings") 14 @input 15 @hint("Label text size (about 44 = 1 cm em height)") 16 @widget(new SliderWidget(40, 300, 1)) 17 labelSize: number = 120 18 19 @ui.group_end 20 21 setup(name: string, detail: string, size: vec3): void { 22 const hx = size.x / 2, hy = size.y / 2, hz = size.z / 2 23 const off = 0.3 24 // -X face (seen from the pallet side while on the shelf): +Z normal rotated to -X 25 this.face("LabelSide", name, detail, new vec3(-hx - off, 0, 0), quat.angleAxis(-Math.PI / 2, vec3.up()), size.z, size.y) 26 // +Z face (near side on the pallet) 27 this.face("LabelFront", name, detail, new vec3(0, 0, hz + off), quat.quatIdentity(), size.x, size.y) 28 // top face, readable from the user's side 29 this.face("LabelTop", name, detail, new vec3(0, hy + off, 0), quat.angleAxis(-Math.PI / 2, vec3.right()), size.x, size.z) 30 } 31 32 private face(objName: string, name: string, detail: string, pos: vec3, rot: quat, w: number, h: number): void { 33 const so = global.scene.createSceneObject(objName) 34 so.setParent(this.sceneObject) 35 so.getTransform().setLocalPosition(pos) 36 so.getTransform().setLocalRotation(rot) 37 const t = so.createComponent("Component.Text") as Text 38 t.text = name + "\n" + detail 39 t.size = this.labelSize 40 t.depthTest = true 41 t.textFill.color = new vec4(1, 1, 1, 1) 42 t.horizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Center 43 t.verticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center 44 t.horizontalOverflow = HorizontalOverflow.Shrink 45 t.verticalOverflow = VerticalOverflow.Shrink 46 const hw = w / 2 - 2 47 const hh = h / 2 - 2 48 t.layoutRect = Rect.create(-hw, hw, -hh, hh) 49 } 50 } 51

#!/bin/sh
# usage: record.sh <scratch dir>; records the Preview region until "[DEMO] end" appears in the LS log after start.
S="$1"; V=/c/Users/Fatal/Desktop/specs_hackathon/pallet_lens/devpost/video
L="C:/Users/Fatal/AppData/Local/Snap/Lens Studio/logs/LensStudioLog-2026-11-08-22-37-48-770-b5e8c.txt"
OFF=$(stat -c %s "$L"); echo "$OFF" > "$S/log_offset.txt"; rm -f "$S/stop.flag"
date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N" > $V/record_start.txt
{ while [ ! -f "$S/stop.flag" ]; do sleep 0.1; done; printf q; sleep 6; } | \
  /c/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe -y -f gdigrab -framerate 30 -offset_x 2292 -offset_y 87 -video_size 1476x830 -draw_mouse 0 -i desktop -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p $V/raw_demo.mp4 > "$S/ffmpeg.log" 2>&1 &
i=0
while [ $i -lt 1500 ]; do   # 5 min cap at 0.2 s
  if tail -c +$((OFF+1)) "$L" | grep -aq "\[DEMO\] end"; then break; fi
  sleep 0.2; i=$((i+1))
done
date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N" > "$S/stop_time.txt"; touch "$S/stop.flag"; wait
echo "ffmpeg exited"; tail -c 300 "$S/ffmpeg.log"

import re,sys
S=sys.argv[1]; V='C:/Users/Fatal/Desktop/specs_hackathon/pallet_lens/devpost/video/'
L="C:/Users/Fatal/AppData/Local/Snap/Lens Studio/logs/LensStudioLog-2026-11-08-22-37-48-770-b5e8c.txt"
off=int(open(S+'/log_offset.txt').read())
st=open(V+'record_start.txt').read().strip().split()[1]
def sec(t):h,m,s=t.split(':');return int(h)*3600+int(m)*60+float(s)
t0=sec(st)
f=open(L,'rb');f.seek(off);txt=f.read().decode('utf-8','replace')
out=[]
for ln in txt.splitlines():
    if '[DEMO]' in ln or '[StackRight]' in ln:
        m=re.match(r'\w (\d+:\d+:\d+\.\d+) ',ln)

        msg=ln[ln.index('] [',ln.index('[Preview'))+2:]; msg=msg[msg.index('] ')+2:]
        out.append('%8.3f  %s  %s'%(sec(m.group(1))-t0,m.group(1),msg))
open(V+'demo_beats.log','w',encoding='utf-8').write('# t (s from record start '+st+')  log time  line\n'+'\n'.join(out)+'\n')

commands.name: ls-clad:lens-studio-router
commands.description: (ls-clad) Front door for any Lens Studio / Specs / Spectacles / Snapchat Lens task — invoke PROACTIVELY at the start of such a conversation, before the user names a skill. Triggers: Specs, Spectacles, AR glasses, Snap Lens, Snapchat lens/camera, Snap camera, Snap mini app, Lens Studio, .esproj, SIK, UI Kit, VirtualScene; asks like 'build/make a specs|spectacles|snapchat <game or app>', 'make a Snap Lens that...', 'prototype an AR experience', 'build a 3D game' in an LS project. ('specs'/'Spectacles' = Snap's AR glasses, not test specs/RSpec; 'snapchat' = a Lens in the camera, not a 3rd-party API.) Gates LS 5.22+ / project / MCP readiness (never scaffolds; if cwd isn't an LS project, asks you to open it and restart the session so MCP is picked up), uses the platform you named (asks Specs vs Snapchat only if you didn't), then routes to the platform workflow.

commands.name: ls-clad:materials
commands.description: (ls-clad) Material creation, configuration, and assignment patterns for Lens Studio scene construction. Use this skill whenever creating materials, setting colors or PBR properties, assigning materials to objects, or debugging material-related rendering issues. Covers the critical distinction between Editor/GraphQL API and Runtime Lens API material access — using the wrong API is a common source of silent failures.

commands.name: ls-clad:mesh-builder-scripting
commands.description: (ls-clad) Runtime MeshBuilder API reference for Lens Studio — construct or mutate meshes from TypeScript (primitive helpers, lathe, extrude, tube, topology examples, dynamic vertex updates, skinned meshes, vertex colors). Use when writing a script that builds or animates geometry at runtime. For author-time static GLB generation (SPECS Text-to-3D / FAST3D / Blender voxel), use `/build-mesh` instead.

commands.name: ls-clad:perfetto-trace-analysis
commands.description: (ls-clad) Analyzes Perfetto (.pftrace) traces for Lens Studio—quick JSON summary first, then optional deep SQL via a persistent trace server. Use when the user mentions .pftrace, Perfetto, Mobile Lens Profiler, Spectacles Monitor traces, frame drops, jank, LAT, or trace performance analysis.

commands.name: ls-clad:physics
commands.description: (ls-clad) Build or debug Lens Studio physics — gravity, collisions, joints, raycast input, trigger zones, force-driven motion, and physics-driven AR (objects colliding with face/hand/world mesh). Use when wiring `BodyComponent`/`ColliderComponent`/`ConstraintComponent`/`WorldComponent`, building ragdolls, vehicles, breakables, or draggable props, debugging tunneling/constraints, or using `Physics.ForceMode`/`createGlobalProbe`/`addPointConstraint`/`WorldSettingsAsset`/`Matter`/`Filter`. Fires on `.esproj` with `Physics.*` or code like `body.addForce`/`probe.rayCast`. SKIP for other engines (Unity, Unreal, three.js, matter.js, Cannon, Rapier, Godot), non-physics LS work (visual-only face mesh, materials, TouchEvent with no body), and Hair/Cloth sim.

commands.name: ls-clad:preview-inspection
commands.description: (ls-clad) Use when inspecting the live Lens Studio preview — querying scene state, discovering objects by component or property, reading transforms / bounds / component values, exploring the scene hierarchy, or capturing orthographic renders. Universal across Specs and Snapchat Lenses. For driving the preview with hand actions (Pinch / Hover / Drag / etc.), use the specs-preview-interaction skill instead.

commands.name: ls-clad:reset-preview-environment
commands.description: (ls-clad) Reset the Lens Studio preview to a clean state before scene generation. Captures a baseline log timestamp. Use before any scene generation task or when starting fresh.

commands.name: ls-clad:scene-construction
commands.description: (ls-clad) Load when constructing or modifying a scene in Lens Studio. Teaches the canonical preset-first workflow (read → presets → re-read → apply → save). Indexes the domain skills (cameras, materials, shaders, VFX, physics).

commands.name: ls-clad:shader-graph
commands.description: (ls-clad) Create or edit custom shaders and shader graphs — `.graphShader` YAML, GLSL code nodes, and library subgraphs.

commands.name: ls-clad:snapchat-project-init
commands.description: (ls-clad) Snapchat (in-camera Lens) project setup — camera tracking mode, preview camera (front/back) and input via PreviewPanelTool, and project target, each inferred from the Lens's intent. Use when setting up or sanity-checking a Snapchat Lens before previewing.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-27-migration
commands.description: (ls-clad) Migrate a Lens project from Spectacles (2024) to SPECS 27 APIs: WebView, Remote Media, Camera, Depth, Motion Controller, SyncKit, VoiceML→ASR, RemoteReferenceAsset→Supabase. Use when migrating or porting a Lens to SPECS 27, or about deprecated APIs.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-build-ui
commands.description: (ls-clad) Build Specs UI in Lens Studio using SpectaclesUIKit (FlexLayout / GridLayout / Frame / BackPlate / Button / Switch / Slider / TextInputField). Use when the user wants to create a UI panel, status HUD, settings screen, media browser, dock, storefront, or any 2D-ish UI rendered in world space. Generates a TypeScript BaseScriptComponent under Assets/Scripts/ and wires it into the scene.
commands.argumentHint: a short description of what to build — for example "a status HUD with a connecting message" or "a settings panel with two toggles and a volume slider"

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-capture-perf-trace
commands.description: (ls-clad) Static ExecuteEditorCode snippets for simultaneous Lens Studio Preview performance traces. Use when recording .pftrace files via preview.profiling.startTrace without helper scripts.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-leaf-install-packages
commands.description: (ls-clad) Verifies the LEAF testing framework is installed in a Lens Studio project and installs it if missing. LEAF ships as a single Leaf package in the Asset Library; matches the SIK version on install. Use before writing or running LEAF tests.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-leaf-run-in-preview
commands.description: (ls-clad) Run LEAF scenarios directly in the Lens Studio Preview panel — opens the LeafPlugin panel, lists scenarios, and runs them via the Lens Studio MCP. The fastest iteration loop during development.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-leaf-write-scenarios
commands.description: (ls-clad) Write LEAF integration test scenarios for Lens Studio Lenses — analyze the project, author scenarios, register them, and attach to the scene. Use when asked to write tests, add tests, create test scenarios, or add LEAF scenarios.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-lens-perf-attribution
commands.description: (ls-clad) Profile and optimize Lens Studio/Specs projects via differential performance sweeps, component toggling, ms/frame attribution, and optimization plans. Use when analyzing Preview performance traces or building simulation harnesses.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-lens-perf-optimize
commands.description: (ls-clad) Iteratively apply Lens Studio performance fixes from specs-lens-perf-attribution output. Dispatches workers per recommendation, validates with visual-parity + re-attribution, commits each kept fix on a new branch, stops on a user-defined condition.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-ndk
commands.description: (ls-clad) Adds a SpecsNDK CoreJs ABI native module into an existing Lens Studio project. Scaffolds C++ and TypeScript NDK controller. Default export is ping(); use --with-rgba-frame for getFrameRGBA().

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-optimize-lens-mesh
commands.description: (ls-clad) Cuts Specs draw calls in a Lens Studio prefab by merging same-material RenderMeshVisuals, then decimating geometry. Trigger on "reduce draw calls", "merge meshes", "optimize this model", "make this Lens faster". Needs Lens Studio MCP.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-preview-interaction
commands.description: (ls-clad) Use when driving the Lens Studio preview with hand actions — Pinch / Hover / Poke / Drag / Gesture / Release / Rotate / Wait — to trigger buttons, manipulate objects, compose multi-step interaction sequences, or verify Lens behavior end-to-end. Specs-only (requires SIK). For scene queries and visual capture, use the preview-inspection skill.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-project-init
commands.description: (ls-clad) Initializes and validates Specs-specific Lens Studio project setup after the /lens-studio-router skill has gated app/project/MCP readiness. Checks project state, Camera setup (Perspective + DeviceTracking World), SIK/UIKit packages, SIK prefab presence, Preview Panel device, and optional generator dependencies such as Blender and Node.js. Reports environment status and auto-fixes Lens Studio project settings where safe.

commands.name: ls-clad:specs-publish
commands.description: (ls-clad) Publish a Specs Lens through preflight, content-rating proposal, project signing-key setup, Lens icon generation, packaging, upload, and review submission. Use for publishing, submitting, releasing, or shipping a Specs Lens.

commands.name: ls-clad:update-lens-packages
commands.description: (ls-clad) Update outdated packages/libraries (SIK, UIKit, SSK, SyncKit) in a Lens Studio project via the Editor API. Use for 'update my packages', 'upgrade SIK', 'update dependencies', 'pull latest SIK', or any package update ask. Requires Lens Studio MCP.

commands.name: ls-clad:verify-preview
commands.description: (ls-clad) Verify, QA, or screenshot a running Lens in the Lens Studio preview. Capture the runtime view, drive an interaction, check logs, and judge the result inline with full code context. Use when asked to verify a Lens, confirm an edit produces the expected runtime behavior, or observe why the preview looks wrong.

commands.name: ls-clad:vfx-graph
commands.description: (ls-clad) Create or edit custom VFX and particle graphs — `.graphVfx` YAML, the Emit/Spawn/Update/Output pipeline, container subgraphs, particle attributes, and helper templates.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Make a new Design artifact from a brief

commands.name: slides
commands.description: Make a new Slides deck artifact from a brief

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

commands.name: schedule

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring

commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.
